title: attention-pipeline-queueing-and-kernel-crosswalk
body:
Purpose:
This is a working log + hypothesis crosswalk for the weird p99 spikes we've observed in the paged-attention + fused-op path on H100 pools. Goal is to 1) isolate whether the extra 0.6-1.2ms p99 comes from kernel scheduling/queueing vs memcopy/host sync, and 2) produce a simple microbench that can reproduce the spike deterministically for CI regression tests.

Summary so far (top-level):
- Observed: steady-state median token latency matches expectations, but p99 climbs by ~25-40% under certain mixtures of batch sizes and sequence lengths.
- Affected path: flashattention (fused matmul+softmax), paged attention path (when kv-cache pages are evicted/loaded), and a new fused-ops schedule we rolled in (opchain-v3).
- Hypotheses: (H1) kernel enqueue/stream contention due to fragmented CUDA streams; (H2) page faulting / GPU DMA spikes when page boundary crosses pinned region; (H3) fused-op schedule occasionally triggers a slow kernel variant selected by heuristics (tile size fallback); (H4) CPU-side serialization when building launch params for very large batches.

Environments tested (hardware/config):
- H100x2 (pools: dedicated-small), driver: 530.41, cuda: 12.2, pytorch: 2.2 (custom runtime), rocm: not used.
- A100-40GB single: driver 525.85 (for cross-check).
- Model proxies: 7B decoder-only (no kv reuse), 13B with kv-cache enabled, quantized fp16 and q4f16 variants.

Quick microbench commands (repro steps):
- baseline script: ./bench/run_attention_trace.sh --model 13B --seq 1024 --bs 4 --kv-paging on --ops opchain-v3 --trace out/trace-$(date +%s).json
- run with nvprof (coarse): nvprof --metrics achieved_occupancy,sm_efficiency --profile-from-start off -- ./bench/runner --cfg ...
- run with CUPTI stream tracing: python tools/cupti_trace.py --pid $(pidof runner) --out cupti.json
- kernel-level: nvtx ranges added in runtime at: runtime/flash/launch.cpp and runtime/paged/kv_manager.cpp (NOTE: add extra NVTX on both host and device streams)

Key observations and raw numbers (representative):
- Baseline (A100, seq=512, bs=8): med=3.2ms/token, p99=6.5ms/token (no paging).
- With paging enabled and opchain-v3 (H100, seq=1024, bs=4): med_token=4.5ms, p99_token=7.8-9.0ms (variable).
- CUPTI trace showed sporadic gaps of 0.7-1.1ms between kernel launches on the same stream, not explained by kernel duration. Gaps line up with host-side memcpy calls and CUDA events.
- nvprof kernel timeline shows occasional switch to a different kernel variant for the same op (e.g., flash_attn_kernel_tile=64x64 vs 128x64) with a wall delta ~0.4ms longer for the smaller tile variant at seq=1024.
- Experiment: pinning the KV page allocator to a dedicated host thread reduced p99 by ~15% in one run (H100 test), suggesting host-side contention contributes but doesn't fully explain worst-case.

Hypothesis details and tests run: 
H1: stream contention / serialization
- Test: forced single-stream vs multi-stream execution. In single-stream mode, median increases slightly but p99 tightens (fewer gaps). In multi-stream mode p99 increases when many small kernels are enqueued concurrently.
- Conclusion: stream fragmentation is a factor. We need better stream assignment heuristics (group small kernels into a single stream, or use CUDA graph capture where possible).

H2: page/DMA spikes on page boundary crossing
- Test: vary page size (64k, 128k, 256k) and alignment of KV chunks. Added instrumentation to kv_manager: log DMA size and alignments.
- Observed: spikes correlate with DMA transfers > 256k combined with concurrent small-kernel bursts. Some H100 PCI-e bursts show higher latency than on A100.
- Conclusion: paging DMA can produce measurable jitter, especially when scheduling aligns with other host work. Consider async prefetching + throttling and spreading DMA across streams.

H3: fallback kernel variant selection
- Test: force kernel selection to largest tile variant unconditionally. Results: p99 reduced by ~10-20% but median slightly worse for low batch sizes (because large tile kernels underutilize SMs at small batch).
- Note: heuristics currently pick a kernel variant based on sequence length and occupancy estimate. But occupancy estimate is stale for mixed batch loads.
- Conclusion: we should add a runtime check to favor consistent kernel selection in steady-state throughput-critical routes, with a fallback schedule during cold-starts.

H4: CPU-side serialization
- Test: profiled host thread building kernel launch params — JSON of param construction shows heavy lock acquisition on a global kernel-factory when many requests arrive. Replacing global lock with per-GPU local pool reduced host-side jitter.
- Conclusion: some portion of p99 is due to CPU-side lock contention. Fix in PR pending (GH:repo/serving-runtime#4271).

Repro microbench matrix (what to run for CI):
- axes: gpu_type (H100/A100), model_size (7B/13B), seq_len (128/512/1024), batch (1/4/8), kv_paging (on/off), ops (opchain-v2/opchain-v3), kernel_force_variant (auto/force-large)
- target: pick 12 combos that historically triggered p99 > baseline. Save traces for each to /bench/ci_traces/.

Instrumentation additions planned:
- Add NVTX annotations around: pager enqueue/dequeue, async memcpy start/end, launch param build, kernel selection decision point.
- Emit a compact CSV line per token that includes: timestamp_us, kernel_name, kernel_variant, stream_id, dma_bytes, host_lock_wait_us, kernel_duration_us. Keep this low-overhead and toggled by env var.

Short-term action items (next 2 weeks):
- [Priya] land host-side lock removal change (PR ready, add unit tests) — GH 4271.
- [Ethan] prototype CUDA-graph capture for steady-state generation path and run on H100 (bench for 2k tokens).
- [Lena] implement KV prefetch backoff: limit concurrent DMA to X KB/ms and measure p99.
- [Diego] add CSV compact traces and wire them into our Bench runner output.
- Run full microbench matrix nightly on dedicated-small pool and upload traces to gcs://redwood-perf/attention/paged-crosswalk/ with TTL 30d.

Longer-term (MVP):
- Decide on a combined strategy: (A) improved stream grouping + CUDA graphs for steady-state, (B) throttled async paging + prefetching timed w.r.t. kernel bursts, (C) deterministic kernel selection policy for production routes. Estimate 4 sprints to stabilize across both H100 and A100.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are device-side page faults possible in our setup (we use pinned host buffers) or is all jitter host-side? We need a driver-level trace to prove.
- Does NUMA on host affect DMA patterns when multiple allocators run on different sockets? (We saw one odd run on a 2-socket devbox).
- Interaction with quantization: q4f16 changes memory footprint and may shift kernel selection thresholds — need to re-calibrate heuristics.

Notes to self (loose):
- If H100 DMA bursts are culprit, try pacing DMA using cudaMemcpyAsync on a dedicated stream and measure effect.
- Consider adding a light-weight background thread that watches trace gaps and flips a 'stable-kernel' hint to the kernel selector when jitter drops below threshold for N seconds.
- We should add a perf regression gate: if nightly p99 > baseline*1.15 for any combo, fail and upload traces to perf-alert channel.

Attachments / commands used / snippets:
- kernel selector snippet (runtime/flash/kernels.cpp): // tile heuristic + fallback
- nvprof timeline screenshot: out/images/nvprof_timeline_20260211.png (pasted local; see trace folder)
- Example compact CSV line: 170/02/11 13:12:22.345,flash_attn,variant=tile64x64,stream=3,dma=0,host_lock=12us,kernel=280us

Final thought:
This is a multi-factor jitter problem — no single silver bullet. Best immediate ROI looks like removing host-side locks + grouping streams for small kernels. Longer-term is a hybrid strategy of deterministic kernel selection + paced DMA prefetching.

If anyone wants to reproduce quickly: ping runtime-perf or run ./bench/run_attention_trace.sh with the flags above (I left verbose logging on by default under PERF_TRACE=1).

-- Priya
